translations.literal: Prince Liu An once urged against attacking Yue: “The Son of Heaven’s arms campaign without needing pitched battle.”
translations.idiomatic: Huainan king Liu An argued imperial armies should awe rather than brawl.

sentences.zh: 言其莫敢校也。

translations.literal: Meaning none dare answer blow for blow.
translations.idiomatic: That is, none dare exchange blows.

sentences.zh: 〔一〕如使越人蒙死以逆執事廝輿之卒，〔二〕有一不備而歸者，雖得越王之首，而猶為大漢羞之。

translations.literal: Commentary mark one commentary mark two If Yue men charged death against our baggage handlers and teamsters with even one line incomplete returning though we took the Yue king’s head it would shame Great Han.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary one two: Risking common soldiers against desperate southerners—even victory humiliates the throne.

sentences.zh: 」而欲以齊民易醜虜，皇威辱外夷，就如其言，猶已危矣，況乎得失不可量邪！

translations.literal: ” Yet trading orderly farmers for ugly barbarians and humbling imperial majesty on barbarians—even granting success—is perilous; how much more when outcomes cannot be reckoned!
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificing settlers to punish nomads dishonors the dynasty regardless of outcome.

sentences.zh: 昔珠崖郡反，孝元皇帝納賈捐之言，而下詔曰：「珠崖背畔，今議者或曰可討，或曰棄之。

translations.literal: When Zhuya commandery rebelled Emperor Yuan accepted Jia Juan’s counsel and issued an edict: “Zhuya turned rebel; advisers split between conquer or abandon.”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan’s Zhuya debate mirrored today—fight or cut loose.

sentences.zh: 朕日夜惟思，羞威不行，則欲誅之；

translations.literal: Day and night I weigh shame if awe fails I wish to punish them;
translations.idiomatic: He burned with shame yet hungered to punish—

sentences.zh: 通于時變，復憂萬民。

translations.literal: reading the moment’s change again I pity the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: but pity for starving subjects outweighed pride.

sentences.zh: 夫萬民之飢與遠蠻之不討，何者為大？

translations.literal: Between starving commoners and unpunished distant barbarians which weighs heavier?
translations.idiomatic: Mass starvation trumped punishing remote rebels.

sentences.zh: 宗廟之祭，凶年猶有不備，況避不嫌之辱哉！

translations.literal: Even ancestral sacrifices lack full offerings in famine years—why cling to a shame one could wisely dodge!
translations.idiomatic: Temple rites shrink in bad harvests; swallowing pointless insults is worse.

sentences.zh: 今關東大困，無以相贍，又當動兵，非但勞民而已。

translations.literal: Now east of the passes lies in dire want with nothing to aid another levy—not mere hardship for commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong starves; fresh armies would break more than peasant backs.

sentences.zh: 其罷珠崖郡。

translations.literal: Therefore abolish Zhuya commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He dissolved Zhuya instead.

sentences.zh: 」此元帝所以發德音也。

translations.literal: ” Thus Yuan Emperor broadcast humane virtue.
translations.idiomatic: That edict defined Emperor Yuan’s mercy.

sentences.zh: 夫卹民救急，雖成郡列縣，尚猶棄之，況障塞之外，未嘗為民居者乎！

translations.literal: Relieving people in crisis—even whole commanderies or counties—Han cast aside; how much more land beyond the barriers never settled by Chinese!
translations.idiomatic: Han surrendered counties to feed people—why obsess over uninhabited desert?

sentences.zh: 守邊之術，李牧善其略，〔三〕保塞之論，嚴尤申其要，〔四〕遺業猶在，文章具存，循二子之策，守先帝之規，臣曰可矣。

translations.literal: Frontier defense: Li Mu perfected the approach commentary mark three garrison policy Yan You distilled the essentials commentary mark four their writings survive—follow those two plans and former emperors’ regulations and this subject says yes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu’s frontier playbook commentary three and Yan You’s garrison theory commentary four remain legible—honor them and rest easy.

sentences.zh: 〔一〕 校，報也。

translations.literal: Commentary mark one xiao means “answer,” resist.
translations.idiomatic: Here xiao means to resist.

sentences.zh: 〔二〕 前書音義曰：「廝，微也。

translations.literal: Commentary mark two Former Han pronunciation gloss: si means petty;
translations.idiomatic: Si denotes menial rank commentary two.

sentences.zh: 輿，眾也。」

translations.literal: The graph yu means “crowd.”
translations.idiomatic: Here yu glosses as “multitude.”

sentences.zh: 〔三〕 史記曰，李牧，趙之北邊良將也。

translations.literal: Commentary mark three Records says Li Mu was Zhao’s stellar northern defender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu held Zhao’s north commentary three.

sentences.zh: 常居代、鴈門備匈奴，以便宜置吏，巿租不入幕府，為士卒費，謹烽火，邊無失亡也。

translations.literal: He stayed in Dai and Yanmen against the Xiongnu, appointed officers as expedient, kept market rents out of headquarters for troop expenses, watched beacon fires—frontier losses vanished.
translations.idiomatic: He fed troops with border tolls, tightened signals, and kept losses near zero.

sentences.zh: 〔四〕 前書王莽發三十萬眾，十道出擊匈奴。

translations.literal: Commentary mark four Former Han records Wang Mang launching three hundred thousand men in ten columns against the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang’s ten-route debacle commentary four proves the cost of blind offensives.

sentences.zh: 莽將嚴尤諫曰：「匈奴為害，所從來久，未聞上代有征之者也。

translations.literal: General Yan You remonstrated: “Harm from the Xiongnu has lasted forever; high antiquity never heard of conquering them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan You told Mang no sage dynasty truly “finished” the nomads.

sentences.zh: 後世三家周、秦、漢征之，然皆未有得上策者也。

translations.literal: Later Zhou Qin and Han campaigned yet none achieved the superior strategy.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qin and Han all fought—and none found the magic formula.”

sentences.zh: 周宣王時獫狁內侵，至于涇陽，命將出征之，盡境而還，是得中策。

translations.literal: Under King Xuan of Zhou the Xianyun pressed inward to Jingyang; he ordered generals on campaign, who drove them out and returned at the border—that was the middling strategy.
translations.idiomatic: King Xuan’s generals pushed the Xianyun back to the frontier and stopped—the classic “middle” option.

sentences.zh: 武帝選將練兵，深入遠戍，兵連禍結三十餘年，是為下策。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu picked generals, drilled troops, penetrated deep with distant garrisons, and chained war to disaster for more than thirty years—that was the inferior strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu’s thirty-year deep offensive was the “low” road—endless war.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇不忍小恥，築長城之固，以喪社稷，是為無策。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang could not stomach slight shame; he piled up the Long Wall’s solidity and forfeited his altars of soil and grain—that was no strategy at all.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor’s wall-building panic destroyed his dynasty—strategy zero.

sentences.zh: 」班固曰：「若乃征伐之功，秦、漢行事，嚴尤論之當也。」

translations.literal: ” Ban Gu said: “As for the merit of campaigns and Qin-Han practice, Yan You’s discussion hits the mark.”
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu adds that Yan You judged Qin-Han frontier policy fairly.

sentences.zh: 〔一〕 左傳曰，楚大夫薳啟彊對楚靈王曰：「晉之事君，臣曰可矣。」

translations.literal: Commentary one: the Zuo zhuan records Chu minister Wei Qiqiang answering King Ling of Chu: “In serving its lord Jin has done enough.”
translations.idiomatic: The gloss cites Wei Qiqiang’s reassurance to Chu about Jin’s loyalty.

sentences.zh: 〔二〕 從音子用反。

translations.literal: Commentary two: cong is read zi-yong fan.
translations.idiomatic: Cong uses the zi-yong fanqie spelling.

sentences.zh: 光和中，檀石槐死，時年四十五，子和連代立。

translations.literal: During the Guanghe era Tanshi Huai died at forty-five; his son Helian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Huai died in Guanghe at forty-five; Helian inherited the confederation.

sentences.zh: 和連才力不及父，亦數為寇抄，性貪淫，斷法不平，眾畔者半。

translations.literal: Helian lacked his father’s vigor yet still raided often; greedy and lecherous, his judgments were unjust and half his people rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Weaker than his father, Helian pillaged anyway until corruption split the tribes.

sentences.zh: 後出攻北地，廉人善弩射者〔一〕射中和連，即死。

translations.literal: Later riding against Beidi, crossbowmen of Lian county commentary one shot Helian and killed him outright.
translations.idiomatic: Beidi crossbowmen from Lian note one dropped Helian with a bolt.

sentences.zh: 其子騫曼年小，兄子魁頭立。

translations.literal: His son Qianman was young, so his cousin Kuitou took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Minor Qianman yielded rule to uncle Kuitou.

sentences.zh: 後騫曼長大，與魁頭爭國，眾遂離散。

translations.literal: When Qianman matured he fought Kuitou for the realm and the tribes scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Adult Qianman’s civil war shattered unity.

sentences.zh: 魁頭死，弟步度根立。

translations.literal: Kuitou died; younger brother Budugen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Kuitou’s death brought Budugen to power.

sentences.zh: 自檀石槐後，諸大人遂世相傳襲。

translations.literal: After Tanshi Huai the great men’s offices passed by hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Huai’s successors turned “great man” into a family title.

sentences.zh: 〔一〕 廉，縣名，屬北地郡。

translations.literal: Commentary one: Lian is a county in Beidi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lian County sat in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 論曰：四夷之暴，其埶互彊矣。

translations.literal: Discourse: the violence of the four barbarians waxed by turns.
translations.idiomatic: The treatise opens: each frontier people surged in its season.

sentences.zh: 匈奴熾於隆漢，西羌猛於中興。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu blazed under Later Han’s zenith; the western Qiang flared during the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongnu peaked in Western Han glory days; Qiang shook the Guangwu revival.

sentences.zh: 而靈獻之閒，二虜迭盛，石槐驍猛，盡有單于之地，蹋頓凶桀，公據遼西之土。

translations.literal: Between Emperors Ling and Xian the two foes flourished in rotation—Shihuai’s valor seized all the old chanyu pasture while Tadun’s cruelty carved Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han saw both steppe powers peak: Huai swallowed Xiongnu ranges; Tadun gripped Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 其陵跨中國，結患生人者，靡世而寧焉。

translations.literal: Those who stride over China binding calamity on the living never left an age undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Their raids scourged the interior generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 然制御上略，歷世無聞；

translations.literal: Yet superior methods of control pass unmentioned across dynasties;
translations.idiomatic: No reign mastered the high policy of restraint;

sentences.zh: 周、漢之策，僅得中下。

translations.literal: Zhou and Han tactics barely reached middle or lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Han settled for middling or poor frontier doctrine.

sentences.zh: 將天之冥數，以至於是乎？

translations.literal: Was it heaven’s hidden decree that it should come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye wonders whether fate doomed the north.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：二虜首施，鯁我北垂。

translations.literal: Encomium: the two foes swayed first and last, blocking our northern rim.
translations.idiomatic: Final stanza: twin barbarian powers choked the northern march.

sentences.zh: 道暢則馴，時薄先離。

translations.literal: When the Way ran clear they grew tame; when seasons thinned they broke away first.
translations.idiomatic: Prosperity bought peace; decline opened rebellion.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial collation section heading.

sentences.zh: 二九七九頁 三行 烏桓者本東胡也 按：魏志「桓」皆作「丸」。

translations.literal: Page 2979 line 3 “The Wuhuan were originally Eastern Hu.” Note: Wei zhi writes the second graph as wan throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Wei chronicles prefer the spelling “Wuwán.”

sentences.zh: 二九七九頁 五行 其性悍塞 按：集解引惠棟說，謂魏書「悍塞」作「悍鷔」。

translations.literal: Page 2979 line 5 “their nature fierce and blocked.” Note: Hui Dong’s commentary cites Wei shu reading “fierce as an owl.”
translations.idiomatic: Variant in Wei documents swaps the second compound graph for “owl-like ferocity.”

sentences.zh: 二九七九頁一二行 簂步搖 按：三國志注引魏書作「冠步搖」。

translations.literal: Page 2979 line 12 “gui buyao.” Note: Three Kingdoms commentary cites Wei shu as “crowned buyao.”
translations.idiomatic: Wei text speaks of buyao crowns rather than gui ornaments.

sentences.zh: 二九八〇頁 一行 實如穄子 按：三國志注引魏書「穄」作「葵」。

translations.literal: Page 2980 line 1 “grain like broomcorn millet.” Note: Three Kingdoms commentary cites Wei shu writing “sunflower” instead of millet.
translations.idiomatic: Wei witnesses read a different grain graph—possibly sunflower seeds.

sentences.zh: 二九八〇頁 六行 簂音

translations.literal: Page 2980 line 6 “gui is read.”
translations.idiomatic: Sound gloss header for gui.

translations.literal: (ji)
translations.idiomatic: (Alternate phonetic marker ji.)

sentences.zh: 〔古〕誨反 按：張森楷校勘記謂吉簂不同母，不得用為反切。

translations.literal: Commentary note: Zhang Senkai’s collation argues ji and gui differ in initial consonants and cannot form a fanqie pair.
translations.idiomatic: Editors flag an impossible fanqie pairing between ji and gui.

sentences.zh: 據廣韻古對切，集韻古獲切，疑此「吉」字亦「古」字之誤。

translations.literal: According to Guangyun gu-dui cut and Jiyun gu-huo cut, suspect this ji graph should also be gu.
translations.idiomatic: Rhyme books suggest ji is a scribal error for gu.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Text amended per above.

sentences.zh: 二九八一頁一四行 遂自亡畔 「自」原作「皆」，逕據汲本、殿本改。

translations.literal: Page 2981 line 14 “thereupon fled rebellion themselves.” Original wrote “all”; emended per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Manuscripts wrongly said “all deserted”; authoritative prints read “themselves.”

sentences.zh: 按：通志亦作「自」。

translations.literal: Note: Tong zhi likewise reads “self.”
translations.idiomatic: Tong zhi agrees with “self.”

sentences.zh: 二九八二頁 七行 郝旦等九百二十二人率眾向化詣闕朝貢至於是封其渠帥為侯王君長者八十一人按：魏志烏丸傳注引魏書，云「烏丸大人郝且等九千餘人，率眾詣闕，封其渠帥為侯王者八十餘人」，與此異。

translations.literal: Page 2982 line 7 “invested their great man Rong Zhuwei…” through “eighty-one channel chiefs.” Note: Wei zhi Wuhuan commentary cites Wei shu with nine thousand followers and eighty-plus kings—differs from Fan Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei shu counts nine thousand courtiers and eighty kings, not Fan Ye’s figures.

sentences.zh: 「郝旦」作「郝且」，旦且形近，未知孰是。

translations.literal: “Hao Dan” versus “Hao Ju”—graphs resemble; unclear which is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Dan and Ju are easily confused in manuscripts.

sentences.zh: 二九八三頁 三行 鴈門烏桓率眾王無何

translations.literal: Page 2983 line 3 “Yanmen Wuhuan prince Wuhe.”
translations.idiomatic: Collation anchor on the Wuhe line.

translations.idiomatic: (Spurious “yun” gloss deleted.)

sentences.zh: 據刊誤刪。

translations.literal: Deleted per Kanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Removed following textual criticism.

sentences.zh: 按：校補謂通志亦無「允」字。

translations.literal: Note: collation supplement says Tong zhi also lacks “yun.”
translations.idiomatic: Tong zhi never carried the extra graph.

sentences.zh: 二九八三頁 五行 拜其大人戎朱廆為親漢都尉 集解引惠棟說，謂續漢書及魏書「朱」作「末」。

translations.literal: Page 2983 line 5 “invested great man Rong Zhuwei.” Hui Dong cites Xu Han shu and Wei shu writing “mo” instead of “zhu.”
translations.idiomatic: Personal name variant Mo versus Zhu in parallel texts.

sentences.zh: 按：校補謂通志亦作「末」。

translations.literal: Note: collation supplement says Tong zhi also writes “mo.”
translations.idiomatic: Tong zhi sides with “mo.”

sentences.zh: 二九八三頁一二行 朔方烏桓與休著屠各並畔 按：「休著屠各」靈帝紀作「休屠各」，南匈奴傳作「休著各」，此「休著屠各」者，錢大昕謂乃讀范史者音著為屠，後遂攙入正文耳。

translations.literal: Page 2983 line 12 “Shuofang Wuhuan with Xiuzhu Tuge revolted.” Note: Lingdi annals write “Xiu Tuge”; Southern Xiongnu treatise “Xiuzhu ge”; Qian Daxin argues readers vocalized zhu as tu and copyists inserted both.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars unpick “Xiuzhu Tuge” as a pronunciation gloss run wild.

sentences.zh: 參閱南匈奴傳校勘記。

translations.literal: See collation notes to Southern Xiongnu treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-reference the southern nomad chapter.

sentences.zh: 二九八三頁一三行 延熹九年夏烏桓復與鮮卑及南匈奴

translations.literal: Page 2983 line 13 “Yanxi ninth year summer Wuhuan again with Xianbei and Southern Xiongnu.”
translations.idiomatic: Collation pinpoints the triple alliance sentence.

sentences.zh: （鮮卑）

translations.literal: (Xianbei)
translations.idiomatic: (Duplicate “Xianbei” bracket suspected.)

sentences.zh: 寇緣邊九郡 按：校補引錢大昭說，謂下「鮮卑」二字疑衍。

translations.literal: “Raid nine frontier commanderies.” Note: collation cites Qian Dazhao—the following “Xianbei” may be redundant.
translations.idiomatic: Editors suspect dittography of “Xianbei.”

sentences.zh: 本紀是年六月南匈奴及烏桓、鮮卑寇緣邊九郡。

translations.literal: Basic annals that year sixth month record Southern Xiongnu plus Wuhuan and Xianbei raiding nine commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial diary lists all three peoples without repetition.

sentences.zh: 今刪。

translations.literal: Now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Excised as redundant.

sentences.zh: 二九八四頁一二行 建安十二年曹操自征烏桓 集解引惠棟說，謂魏書作「十一年」。

translations.literal: Page 2984 line 12 “Jian’an twelfth year Cao Cao personally campaigned against Wuhuan.” Hui Dong cites Wei shu placing it in year eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Wei shu misdates Cao’s expedition one year early.

sentences.zh: 今按魏志武紀在建安十二年夏，魏志烏丸傳作「十一年」，誤。

translations.literal: Checked against Wei Annals—twelfth summer is correct; Wei Wuhuan biography’s “eleventh” is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu ji confirms twelfth year; Wuhuan chapter errs.

sentences.zh: 二九八五頁 二行 原羊 按：殿本考證謂何焯校本「原」改「羱」。

translations.literal: Page 2985 line 2 “yuan sheep.” Note: palace collation says He Zhuo’s manuscript changes yuan to ram-graph.
translations.idiomatic: Some editors read the beast as a wild ram species.

sentences.zh: 二九八五頁 九行 鮮卑始通驛使 按：刊誤謂「驛」當作「譯」。

translations.literal: Page 2985 line 9 “Xianbei first opened post relays.” Note: Kanwu says yi should read yi “interpreter.”
translations.idiomatic: Should read “interpreter envoys,” not “post horses.”

sentences.zh: 二九八五頁一一行 北匈奴左伊育訾部 按：集解引惠棟說，謂祭肜傳「育」作「秩」。

translations.literal: Page 2985 line 11 “Northern Xiongnu left Wing Yuyuzi tribe.” Note: Hui Dong cites Zhai Tong biography writing “秩.”
translations.idiomatic: Parallel passage uses a different graph for the tribal name.

sentences.zh: 二九八五頁一二行 三十年 按：集解引惠棟說，謂袁紀作「三十一年」。

translations.literal: Page 2985 line 12 “thirtieth year.” Note: Hui Dong cites Yuan ji as thirty-first.
translations.idiomatic: Chronicle variant thirty-first year.

sentences.zh: 二九八五頁一三行 歆志賁 按：殿本考證謂魏志注「歆」作「欽」。

translations.literal: Page 2985 line 13 “Xin Zhiben.” Note: Wei commentary writes “Qin.”
translations.idiomatic: Wei text prefers Qin over Xin for the chief’s name.

sentences.zh: 二九八六頁 五行 延平元年 按：集解引王補說，謂「延平」上應有「殤帝」二字。

translations.literal: Page 2986 line 5 “Yanping first year.” Note: Wang Bu argues “Emperor Shang” should precede Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Should specify Emperor Shang’s Yanping reign.

sentences.zh: 二九八七頁一〇行 故城在今營州東〔南〕 據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Page 2987 line 10 “ruins southeast of Yingzhou.” Supplemented per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Direction particle “south” restored from better editions.

sentences.zh: 二九八八頁 四行 殺漸將王 按：殿本「漸」作「斬」。

translations.literal: Page 2988 line 4 “killed the gradual general king.” Note: Palace writes zhan “decapitate.”
translations.idiomatic: Palace edition swaps similar graphs—likely “decapitate.”

sentences.zh: 參閱南匈奴傳校勘記。

translations.literal: See collation notes to Southern Xiongnu treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-reference southern nomad collation.

sentences.zh: 二九八八頁 七行 獲其資重二千餘種 按：校補謂「種」疑當作「輛」。

translations.literal: Page 2988 line 7 “captured their baggage two thousand kinds.” Note: supplement suspects zhong should read liang “wagonloads.”
translations.idiomatic: Probably “two thousand carts,” not “kinds.”

sentences.zh: 二九八八頁 八行 牛馬什物 按：殿本作「牛羊財物」。

translations.literal: Page 2988 line 8 “cattle horse miscellany.” Note: Palace reads “sheep cattle wealth.”
translations.idiomatic: Palace wording shifts livestock list.

sentences.zh: 二九八八頁一三行 耿曄遣烏桓親漢都尉戎朱廆率眾王侯咄歸等 按：刊誤謂魏志此「眾」字作「將」字，言率將胡王等出塞，後乃封為率眾王侯長也。

translations.literal: Page 2988 line 13 “Geng Ye sent Colonel-close-to-Han Rong Zhuwei leading prince-dukes Zhu Gui…” Note: Kanwu says Wei zhi writes “general” for “masses,” meaning he led barbarian kings before they earned “prince of masses” titles.
translations.idiomatic: Wei wording distinguishes general-led raid from later ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 二九八八頁一五行 匈奴中郎將趙稠 按：沈家本謂「趙稠」紀作「王稠」。

translations.literal: Page 2988 line 15 “Chief Commander of Xiongnu Zhao Chou.” Shen Jiaben says annals write Wang Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Annals carry Wang Chou instead of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 「匈奴」上奪「使」字。

translations.literal: The verb “sent” is missing before “Xiongnu.”
translations.idiomatic: Restored missing shi “dispatch.”

sentences.zh: 二九八九頁 七行 彈汗山 按：集解引惠棟說，謂「汗」通鑑作「汙」。

translations.literal: Page 2989 line 7 “Mount Tanhan.” Note: Hui Dong cites Zizhi tongjian writing “Tanwu.”
translations.idiomatic: Tongjian prefers Tanwu spelling.

sentences.zh: 二九九一頁 三行 〔封〕丞相為富人侯 據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Page 2991 line 3 “enfeoff chancellor as Rich Marquis.” Supplemented per Ji and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: Missing “enfeoff” restored from reliable prints.

sentences.zh: 二九九一頁 四行 夫以世宗神武 張森楷校勘記謂群書治要「世宗」作「武帝」，是知范書原文作「武帝」，後人妄以武帝本是世宗，唐避諱改，遂回改為「世宗」，而不知非也。

translations.literal: Page 2991 line 4 “As for Shizong’s divine arms.” Zhang Senkai argues Qunshu zhiyao writes “Emperor Wu,” proving Fan Ye originally said Emperor Wu and later editors wrongly substituted the temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Tang excerpt preserves “Emperor Wu”; “Shizong” may be a misguided restoration.

sentences.zh: 今按：邕集作「世宗」。

translations.literal: Checked: Cai Yong’s collected works still read “Shizong.”
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cai Yong’s own corpus keeps Shizong.

sentences.zh: 二九九一頁 四行 將相良猛 按：汲本、殿本「相」作「帥」。

translations.literal: Page 2991 line 4 “generals and ministers bold.” Note: Ji and Palace write “marshals.”
translations.idiomatic: Variant graph “marshal” versus “minister.”

sentences.zh: 二九九一頁 六行 釱左趾 按：「釱」原作「

translations.literal: Page 2991 line 6 “fetters on left foot.” Note: original wrote obscure compound graph “metal dog.”
translations.idiomatic: Damaged graph described metal fetters.

translations.idiomatic: (Composite glyph for ankle fetters.)

translations.idiomatic: Corrected to standard di graph.

sentences.zh: 二九九二頁 七行 天設山河 按：校補謂通志「山河」作「沙漠」。

translations.literal: Page 2992 line 7 “Heaven set mountains and rivers.” Note: collation supplement cites Tong zhi “desert.”
translations.idiomatic: Tong zhi reads “desert” instead of mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 一九九二頁 八行 豈與蟲螘

translations.literal: Page 1992 line 8 “how could one still with worm-ant.”
translations.idiomatic: Collation addresses gnats-and-ants passage—likely typo in pagination (1992 vs 2992).

translations.idiomatic: (Editorial siglum between graphs.)

sentences.zh: 〔狡〕寇計爭往來哉 校補謂「校」為「狡」之訛。

translations.literal: “crafty foes vie endlessly.” Collation supplement says jiao was corrupted from xiao “school.”
translations.idiomatic: Copyists misread “crafty” as “school.”

sentences.zh: 並引柳從辰說，謂蔡邕集「校」作「狡」。

translations.literal: Also cites Liu Chenchen: Cai Yong anthology writes “crafty.”
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong’s literary collection confirms “crafty.”

translations.literal: Now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Text updated to crafty reading.
